claims.text: Premelting and melting in high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles are governed by a balance between nanoscale surface effects and configurational-entropy-related internal lattice stabilization.
Nanoscale surface effects lower the onset temperature of melting.
Reduced coordination of nanoparticle surface atoms enhances their mobility and causes early surface premelting.
High configurational entropy stabilizes the nanoparticle interior and delays complete melting.
Random multielement alloying in HEA nanoparticles induces lattice strain and bonding heterogeneity.
The lattice strain and heterogeneity of HEA nanoparticles raise the energy barrier for complete melting.
The competition between surface-driven melting depression and internal stabilization makes the HEA melting transition more gradual.
HEA nanoparticles should have an overall higher or delayed complete-melting transition compared with similarly sized conventional nanoparticles.
HEA nanoparticles should begin surface premelting at a lower temperature than similarly sized monometallic or binary nanoparticles.
Conventional monometallic or binary nanoparticles should melt more sharply than HEA nanoparticles.
Homogeneous supported HEA nanoparticles containing five to ten elements can be synthesized by rapid high-temperature processing.
The proposed HEA nanoparticles may be equimolar or near-equimolar mixtures of at least five metals.
The proposed mechanism should hold from a few nanometers up to approximately 100 nm.
The proposed mechanism should operate from room temperature to temperatures near the bulk melting points of the constituent metals.
Support anchoring and nanoparticle-support interactions can modify nanoparticle thermal stability.
The governing factor can be tested by heating HEA and conventional nanoparticles with matched size distributions, morphologies, supports, atmospheres, and heating rates.
In situ TEM or DSC can be used to compare the onset of surface disordering, complete melting temperature, and transition gradualness.
Failure to observe lower premelting onset or delayed and more gradual complete melting in HEA nanoparticles would falsify the proposed interplay mechanism.
